questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding orographic rainfall is correct?

options.text: This precipitation is heavy but of short duration, highly localised and is associated with minimum amount of cloudiness.
This type of precipitation occurs when warm, humid air strikes on a mountain range.
This type of precipitation is characterised by seasonal reversal of winds that carry oceanic moisture.
It occurs mainly during summer and is common over equatorial doldrums in the Congo basin.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**This type of precipitation occurs when warm, humid air strikes on a mountain range.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Orographic rainfall occurs when moist air is forced to ascend over a mountain range.
 
• As the air rises, it cools and condenses to form clouds, leading to precipitation.
 
• This type of rainfall is common in mountainous regions such as the Western Ghats in India and the Andes in South America.
 
• The windward side of the mountain receives heavy rainfall, while the leeward side (rain shadow area) receives very little.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Orographic Rainfall**

 
 
• Orographic rainfall is a type of precipitation induced by the presence of elevated terrain such as mountains.
 
• When warm, humid air is forced to rise over a mountain range, it cools and loses its capacity to hold moisture, leading to cloud formation and precipitation.
 
• This phenomenon is common in coastal mountain ranges where moist winds from oceans or seas are forced to rise.
 
• The windward side of the mountain receives heavy rainfall, whereas the leeward side, known as the rain shadow area, receives significantly less rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Types of Rainfall**
 
 
• **Convectional Rainfall:** Occurs due to intense heating of the Earth's surface, leading to the rising of warm, moist air which then cools and condenses to form rain. Common in equatorial regions.
 
• **Frontal Rainfall:** Occurs when warm air mass meets a cold air mass, causing the warm air to rise over the cold air, leading to cooling, condensation, and precipitation. Common in mid-latitudes.
 
• **Cyclonic Rainfall:** Associated with cyclones or low-pressure systems, where warm, moist air rises and cools, leading to cloud formation and precipitation. Common in tropical and temperate regions.

questions.question: What type of precipitation is common at the equatorial depression in the Congo Basin, the Amazon Basin, and the islands of Southeast Asia?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Conventional precipitation'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Conventional Precipitation:**

 
 
• Conventional precipitation, also known as convective rainfall, is common in equatorial regions such as the Congo Basin, the Amazon Basin, and the islands of Southeast Asia.
 
• This type of precipitation occurs due to the intense solar heating at the equator, which causes the surface air to warm rapidly and rise.
 
• As the warm, moist air rises, it cools and condenses to form large cumulus clouds, ultimately leading to heavy rainfall.
 
• This phenomenon is frequent in the afternoon or early evening, producing short but intense rain showers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Monsoonal Precipitation:**

 
 
• This type of precipitation is associated with the seasonal wind patterns known as monsoons, typically affecting regions such as South Asia.
 
• Monsoonal precipitation occurs due to the shifting wind patterns that bring moist air from the oceans inland during the summer, leading to heavy and prolonged rainfall.
 
• While the Congo Basin, Amazon Basin, and Southeast Asia experience seasonal variations, they are primarily influenced by equatorial heat rather than monsoon winds.
 
 
 
• **Orographic Precipitation:**
 
 
• Orographic precipitation occurs when moist air is forced to ascend over mountain ranges, cooling and condensing to produce rain.
 
• This type of rainfall is prevalent in regions with significant topographical features such as the Andes or the Himalayas.
 
• In contrast, the Congo Basin and Amazon Basin are relatively flat, and the islands of Southeast Asia experience orographic effects locally but not uniformly across the region.
 
 
 
• **Frontal Precipitation:**
 
 
• Frontal precipitation happens when different air masses meet, leading to the formation of fronts and subsequent rainfall.
 
• This phenomenon commonly occurs in temperate regions where cold and warm fronts frequently interact.
 
• Equatorial regions like the Congo and Amazon Basins, as well as Southeast Asian islands, experience less influence from fronts compared to temperate zones.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Conventional precipitation is critical for maintaining the lush, dense vegetation typical of equatorial rainforests.
 
• This type of rainfall pattern contributes to the high biodiversity and complex ecosystems found in these regions.
 
• The regular occurrence of conventional precipitation is a key factor in shaping the climate and weather patterns of equatorial areas.

questions.question: Cirrus and cumulus are types of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Clouds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Clouds**

 
 
• Clouds help regulate Earth's temperature.
 
• They bring rain to different regions.
 
• Clouds develop out of the process of changing moisture from a gas to liquid through a process called convection.
 
• There are three forms of clouds
 
 

 
• **Cirrus:** curly or fibrous
 
• **Stratus:** sheets or layers
 
• **Cumulus: **Heaped or piled

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil**

 
 
• Soils are a complex mixture of water, air, minerals, and a number of organisms that are decaying.
 
• It forms at the surface of the land.
 
• It is the skin of the earth.
 
• It is capable of supporting plant life and is vital to life on earth.
 
• It is classified into four types:
 
 

 
• Sandy Soil
 
• Silt Soil
 
• Clay Soil
 
• Loamy Soil

 
• **Mountains**

 
 
• It is an elevated portion of the Earth's crust generally with steep sides.
 
• Forces inside and outside the earth manage the shape of the earth's surface.
 
• There are four types of mountains:
 
 

 
• Volcanic Mountains
 
• F old Mountains
 
• Block Mountain
 
• Residual Mountains

questions.question: According to the Köppen classification, which letter code represents a tropical climate with a dry winter season found in large parts of peninsular India south of the Tropic of Cancer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aw.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aw** represents a tropical climate with a** dry winter season **found in large parts of peninsular India south of the **Tropic of Cancer.**
 
• Climates are classified according to **Köppen's five primary groups**, with **seasonal precipitation** and** temperature** patterns serving as the basis for group divisions.
 
• A stands for** tropical,** B for **desert**, C for **temperate**, D for **continental,** and E for **polar.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **CWh** represents a **subtropical climate** with **dry winters and hot summers**, found in regions with **mild to moderate rainfall **and **high humidity.**
 
• **Dw** represents a severe continental climate with **dry winters and hot summers,** found in regions with** low precipitation** and** large temperature** fluctuations between seasons.

questions.question: The ______ layer starts at Earth's surface and extends 8 to 14.5 km high (5 to 9 miles). This part of the atmosphere is the densest and almost all weather is in this region.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Troposphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The air is one of the essential conditions for the existence of life on this planet. The air is a mixture of various gases and it encompasses the earth from all sides. The air surrounding the earth is called the atmosphere.**
 
• **Troposphere**:
 
 
• It is the lowermost layer of the atmosphere.
 
• The layer starts at Earth's surface and extends 8 to 14.5 km high (5 to 9 miles).
 
• The troposphere contains dust particles and water vapour.
 
• This is the most important layer of the atmosphere because all kinds of weather changes take place only in this layer.
 
• The zone dividing troposphere from the stratosphere is known as the tropopause.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Stratosphere:

 
 
• ​It lies beyond troposphere, up to an altitude of 50 km from the earth’s surface.
 
• The temperature in this layer remains constant for some distance but then rises to reach a level of 0°C at 50 km altitude.
 
• This rise is due to the presence of ozone.
 
• This layer is almost free from clouds and associated weather phenomenon, making conditions most ideal for flying aeroplanes. ​
 
 
 
• Mesosphere: 
 
 
• ​This is an intermediate layer beyond the ozone layer and continues up to an altitude of 80 km from the earth’s surface.
 
• The temperature gradually falls to -100°C at 80 km altitude.
 
• Meteorites burn up in this layer on entering from the space.
 
 
 
• Thermosphere:
 
 
• ​In the thermosphere, the temperature rises very rapidly with increasing height.
 
• The ionosphere is a part of this layer.
 
• It extends between 80-400 km. This layer helps in radio transmission.
 
 
 
• Exosphere:​
 
 
• This is the uppermost layer of the atmosphere extending beyond the ionosphere above a height of about 400 km.
 
• The air is extremely rarefied and the temperature gradually increases through the layer.
 
• Light gases like helium and hydrogen float into space from here.

questions.question: The Himalayan Mountains act as an effective climatic divide by protecting the subcontinent from:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cold northern winds.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Himalayan Mountains** are the highest mountain range in the world and act as a **natural barrier** that separates the Indian subcontinent from the rest of Asia.
 
• The mountains act as an effective** climatic divide** by protecting the subcontinent from the** cold northern winds** that blow from the** Tibetan Plateau** and **Central Asia.**
 
• The Himalayas also block the** warm southern winds** that originate from the **Indian Ocean**, preventing them from entering the subcontinent and making the climate cooler and drier.
 
• Cyclonic winds are **not affected** by the Himalayan Mountains and can still enter the subcontinent, causing** heavy rainfall and flooding** in some regions.
 
• **Western disturbances** are weather systems that originate from the** Mediterranean region** and can enter the subcontinent from the northwest, but their impact is reduced by the Himalayan Mountains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Himalayan Mountains are located in the **northern part of the Indian subcontinent** and stretch over **2,400 km** from **Afghanistan to Myanmar.**
 
• The mountains are home to some of the highest peaks in the world, including **Mount Everest,** which is the highest peak at 8,848 meters.
 
• The Himalayas are also the source of many major rivers in** South Asia,** including the** Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Indus rivers.**
 
• **Cyclonic winds **are **low-pressure systems** that form over warm ocean waters and can cause** heavy rainfall and strong winds **when they make landfall.
 
 
• They are common in the** Bay of Bengal** and the** Arabian Sea.**
 
 
 
• Western disturbances are weather systems that **bring rain and snow **to the western Himalayan region from November to April.
 
 
• They are important for** agriculture and water supply** in the region.

questions.question: According to Köppen's climate classification scheme, dry climates are subdivided using the capital letter S for semi-arid regions or steppe and W for ________ region.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Desert.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to Köppen's climate classification scheme, dry climates are subdivided using the capital letter S for semi-arid regions or steppe and W for the **desert regions.**
 
• **Dry climates **are divided into **steppe or semi-arid climates (BS) and ****desert climates (BW)**.
 
• They are further subdivided as subtropical steppe (BSh) and subtropical desert (BWh) at latitudes from 15° - 35° and mid-latitude steppe (BSk) and mid-latitude desert (BWk) at latitudes between 35° - 60°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Koeppen climate classification system recognizes **five major climatic types and each type is designated by a capital letter- A, B, C, D, E, and H.**
 
• The seasons of dryness are indicated by the **small letters: f, m, w, and s.**
 
• The small letters a, b, c, and d refer to the degree of severity of temperature.
 
• The five main groups are **A (tropical), B (dry), C (temperate), D (continental), and E (polar).**
 
• Each group and subgroup is represented by a letter. All climates are assigned a main group (the first letter). All climates except for those in the E group are assigned a seasonal precipitation subgroup (the second letter).

questions.question: In which layer of atmosphere does the meteorites burn up on entering from the space?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mesosphere**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Mesosphere:

__
 
• It lies above the stratosphere, which extends up to a height of 80 km.
 
• In this layer, once again, the temperature starts decreasing with the increase in altitude and reaches up to minus 100°C at a height of 80 km.
 
• Meteorites burn up in this layer on entering from space.
 
• The upper limit of the mesosphere is known as mesopause.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Stratosphere:

 
• It is the second major strata of air in the atmosphere.
 
• It is found above the tropopause and extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• One important feature of the stratosphere is that it contains the ozone layer.
 
• This layer absorbs ultra-violet radiation and shields life on the earth from an intense, harmful form of energy.
 
• The air temperature in the stratosphere remains relatively constant up to an altitude of 15 miles (25 km).
 
• Then it increases gradually to up to stratopause. 

Troposphere:

 
• It is the lowermost layer of the atmosphere.
 
• Its average height is 13 km and extends roughly to a height of 8 km near the poles and about 18 km at the equator.
 
• The thickness of the troposphere is greatest at the equator because heat is transported to great heights by strong convectional currents.
 
• This layer contains dust particles and water vapour.
 
• All changes in climate and weather take place in this layer.
 
• The temperature in this layer decreases at the rate of 1°C for every 165m of height.
 
• This is the most important layer for all biological activity.

​Thermosphere 

 
• It is located between 80 and 400 km above the mesopause.
 
• It contains electrically charged particles known as ions, and hence, it is also known as the ionosphere.
 
• Radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
 
• This layer helps in the transmission of radio waves.
 
• The temperature here starts increasing with height.

Exosphere:

 
• It is the uppermost layer of the atmosphere.
 
• This is the highest layer but very little is known about it.
 
• Whatever contents are there, these are extremely rarefied in this layer, and it gradually merges with outer space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aac671501024a6da0309f9a49fe34b0d0064aba58026951c96927ee90b0dd7a8.png]

questions.question: Most of the atmospheric Ozone gas is found in which layer of the atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Stratosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Ninety percent of the ozone gas in the atmosphere is occupied by the stratosphere, the layer of the atmosphere between about 10 and 50 kilometers altitude. **
 
• The natural level of ozone gas in the stratosphere is a result of a balance between sunlight that **creates ozone gas and chemical reactions that destroy it.**
 
• The Earth's atmosphere consists of several layers.
 
 
• The lowest layer, the troposphere, extends from the Earth's surface up to about **10 kilometers **in altitude. 
 
• The next layer, the stratosphere, continues from 10 km to about 50 km. 
 
• **Ozone is a molecule that contains three oxygen atoms**.
 
 
• ** Ozone molecules are constantly formed and destroyed in the stratosphere**. 
 
• The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs a portion of the radiation from the sun, preventing it from reaching the planet's surface. 
 
• It absorbs the portion of the UV light called UVB.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Thermosphere:-**

 
• **The thermosphere is the layer in the Earth's atmosphere directly above the mesosphere and below the exosphere. **
 
• Within this layer of the atmosphere, ultraviolet radiation causes photoionization/photodissociation of molecules, creating ions, the thermosphere thus constitutes the larger part of the ionosphere.

**Mesosphere:-**

 
• **The mesosphere is directly above the stratosphere and below the thermosphere**.
 
• It extends from about 31 to 53 miles above our planet.
 
• Temperature decreases with height throughout the mesosphere.

**Troposphere:-**

 
• **The troposphere is the lowest layer of Earth's atmosphere and the site of all weather on Earth**.
 
• The troposphere is bounded on the top by a layer of air called the tropopause, which separates the troposphere from the stratosphere, and on the bottom by the surface of the Earth.

questions.question: Which statement best explains why Shillong gets around 200 cm rainfall annually; whereas Cherrapunji, which is around 30 km away (as the crow ﬂies), gets over 1250 cm of rainfall annually?

options.text: Cherrapunji lies on the windward side of the Khasi hills and receives rainfall from the Bay of Bengal branch of monsoon, while Shillong lies on the leeward side of the Khasi hills, which forms the rain shadow area.
Cherrapunii gets rainfall from rain-laden clouds coming from the Himalayas, whereas Shillong gets rainfall from the Malabar branch of monsoon.
Cherrapunji lies on the leeward side of the Khasi hills and Shillong lies on the windward side of the Khasi hills, and thus, gets only wind and no rain.
The average temperature of Shillong has gone up due to excessive deforestation and pollution.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cherrapunji lies on the windward side of the Khasi hills and receives rainfall from the Bay of Bengal branch of monsoon, while Shillong lies on the leeward side of the Khasi hills, which forms the rain shadow area.**__

 
• The highest rainfall in India is at **Cherrapunji(Present name Sohra) in Mawsynram village of Meghalaya state.**
 
• The Average rainfall of Cherrapunji is **11,777 mm or 463.7 inches.**
 
• Mawsynram is located in the **East Khasi Hills district.**
 
• It is on the **windward side of the hills** and is surrounded by hills on three sides.
 
• It receives rain from **southwest monsoon winds** (Bay of Bengal branch), as the winds cannot move further striking the hills and due to condensation receives heavy rainfall.
 
• Shillong lies on the **northern leeward slopes of the Khasi Hills** and therefore receives less rain.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the Indian monsoon and the Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)?

options.text: The shift in the position of the ITCZ can influence the monsoon patterns in India.
ITCZ is located in the Indo-Gangetic plains during February.
The ITCZ is a phenomenon that occurs only during winter.
The ITCZ has no impact on the Indian monsoon.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The shift in the position of the ITCZ can influence the monsoon patterns in India.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The (ITCZ) is a belt of low pressure near the equator where trade winds from the **Northern and Southern** Hemispheres come together.
 
• The shift in the position of the ITCZ can influence the **monsoon patterns** in India because it determines the location of the monsoon trough, which is a region of** low pressure** that attracts moisture from the surrounding areas.
 
• During summer, the ITCZ shifts northward towards the** Himalayas**, bringing moisture-laden winds from the **Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal **to India, resulting in the monsoon season.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ITCZ is typically located over the** southern Indian Ocean** during this time.
 
• ITCZ is present **throughout the year,** but its position shifts with the seasons.
 
• ITCZ has a significant impact on the** Indian monsoon.**
 
• The** monsoon** is the buildup of **moist clouds **when moisture is released from the atmosphere as it cools down in the form of precipitation.
 
• The ITCZ is the region of the earth where **air convergence** is primarily observed throughout the year.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a permanent wind?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Loo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Permanent winds are those that persist throughout the year and are associated with the Earth's atmospheric circulation system. 
 
• They help to distribute heat, moisture, and air masses across the planet, playing a crucial role in shaping global climate patterns.

​**Loo**__

__
 
• **Loo **is not type of permanent wind.
 
• It is a strong, dry and hot afternoon wind from the west in the summer, blowing over the western Indo-Gangetic Plain region of North India and Pakistan.
 
• It is particularly strong in the months of May and June.
 
• Exposure to it also leads to lethal heat strokes because of its extremely high temperatures (45 °C–50 °C or 115 °F-120 °F).
 
• The technical words that signify the direction in which the wind is blowing are 'Windward' and 'leeward.'
 
• The direction upwind from the point of reference is windward.
 
• Loo has extended its reach and has now gripped more parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and even West Madhya Pradesh. Moreover, some parts of this region are also reeling under heat wave conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** The example of permanent wind are Trade winds, Westerlies and Easterlies.

 
• Trade winds: These are consistent, prevailing winds that blow from the northeast in the Northern Hemisphere and the southeast in the Southern Hemisphere, found between approximately 30° latitude and the equator in both hemispheres.
 
• Westerlies: These winds blow from the southwest in the Northern Hemisphere and the northwest in the Southern Hemisphere, generally found between latitudes 30° and 60° in both hemispheres.
 
• Easterlies: Also known as polar easterlies, these winds blow from the east near the Earth's poles and are formed as cold air masses move away from the poles towards the lower latitudes..

questions.question: What is the average height of troposphere?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The troposphere is the lowest layer of the Earth's atmosphere**, extending from the surface up to an average altitude of about **7 to 12 kilometers (4.3 to 7.5 miles).**
 
• The height of the troposphere varies depending on the location, season, and weather conditions. However, the average height of the troposphere is about **11 kilometers (6.8 miles) above sea level**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earth's atmosphere** can be divided into **five primary layers **based on **their temperature and altitude**:

 
 
• **Troposphere**: This is the lowest layer of the Earth's atmosphere, extending from the surface up to an average altitude of 12 kilometers (7.5 miles) at the equator. The majority of Earth's weather occurs in this layer, and it is where most of the Earth's greenhouse gases are concentrated.
 
• **Stratosphere**: This layer lies above the troposphere, extending from about 12 to 50 kilometers (7.5 to 31 miles) in altitude. The ozone layer is located in this layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun.
 
• Mesosphere: Above the stratosphere, the mesosphere extends from about 50 to 85 kilometers (31 to 53 miles) in altitude. This layer is known for its extremely low temperatures, as low as -100°C (-148°F) at the top.
 
• **Thermosphere**: This layer extends from about 85 kilometers (53 miles) to the edge of space, around 600 kilometers (372 miles) above the Earth's surface. The temperature increases with altitude in this layer, reaching up to 2,000°C (3,632°F) due to the absorption of solar radiation.
 
• **Exosphere:** The outermost layer of Earth's atmosphere, the exosphere, begins at an altitude of about 600 kilometers (372 miles) and extends into space. This layer is where the Earth's atmosphere gradually thins out and merges with the vacuum of space.

questions.question: Which of the following earthquake waves are longitudinal waves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The longitudinal waves, a**lso known as compressional waves or primary waves, are represented by the letter** "P."**
 
• **P waves** are the **fastest seismic waves **and can travel through **solid, liquid, and gas.**
 
• They cause particles to move in the same direction as the wave **propagation, creating a push-pull motion.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b07fabb6b94aa7f0a1469361bcb30cf0b9d3baa03a1911f5c4f76965ea88b5bc.png] 

 

 
• ** P waves (Primary waves):**

 
 
• Also known as **compressional waves.**
 
• Longitudinal waves that travel through the** Earth's interior.**
 
• They cause particles to compress and expand in the same direction as the wave travels.
 
• Can travel through **solid, liquid, and gas.**
 
• **Fastest seismic waves.**
 
• First waves to be recorded by **seismographs.**
 
 
 
• **S waves (Secondary waves):**
 
 
• Also known as **shear waves.**
 
• Transverse waves that travel through the **Earth's interior.**
 
• They cause particles to move perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• Can** only travel through solids.**
 
• **Slower than P waves.**
 
• S**econd waves to be recorded by seismographs.**
 
 
 
• **L waves (Love waves):**
 
 
• Surface waves that travel along the **Earth's surface.**
 
• Named after** A.E.H. Love, who mathematically** described their behavior.
 
• They cause particles to move in a **horizontal, side-to-side motion.**
 
• **Slower than P and S waves.**
 
• Responsible for the most significant damage during an earthquake.
 
 
 
• **N waves (Rayleigh waves):**
 
 
• Surface waves that travel along the **Earth's surface.**
 
• Named after** Lord Rayleigh, **who mathematically described their behavior.
 
• They cause particles to move in an **elliptical motion**, with both vertical and** horizontal components.**
 
• **Slower than P and S waves.**
 
• Can cause vertical ground displacement and **rolling motion.**

__
 
• **The statement "It lies above the mesosphere" **is incorrect when referring to the stratosphere.
 
• The stratosphere is actually located above the troposphere, which is the lowest layer of the **Earth's atmosphere.**
 
• The stratosphere extends from about 10 to 50 kilometers (6 to 31 miles) above the Earth's surface.

The troposphere is where weather phenomena occur, and it contains most of the Earth's air mass and moisture.
 
• **Stratosphere: **Above the troposphere lies the stratosphere, extending from the top of the troposphere up to approximately 50 kilometers (31 miles) in altitude. The stratosphere contains the ozone layer, which plays a crucial role in absorbing the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation.

Despite the high temperatures, the thermosphere would not feel hot to human perception due to its extremely low density of particles.

The exosphere consists of extremely sparse gas molecules that gradually dissipate into the vacuum of outer space.

__
 
• The uppermost layer of the atmosphere above the thermosphere is known as the** exosphere.**
 
• This is the highest layer but very little is known about it.
 
• Whatever contents are there, these are extremely rarefied in this layer, and it gradually merges with the outer space. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The atmosphere consists of different layers with varying densities and temperatures.
 
• Density is highest near the surface of the earth and decreases with increasing altitude.
 
• The column of the atmosphere is divided into five different layers depending upon the temperature condition.
 
• They are the** troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere, and exosphere**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Troposphere**

 
 
• The troposphere is the lowermost layer of the atmosphere.
 
• Its average height is 13 km and extends roughly to a height of 8 km near the poles and about 18 km at the equator.
 
 
 
• **Stratosphere **
 
 
• The stratosphere is found above the tropopause and extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• The stratosphere contains the ozone layer.
 
 
 
• **Mesosphere**
 
 
• The mesosphere lies above the stratosphere, which extends up to a height of 80 km.
 
• In this layer, the temperature starts decreasing with the increase in altitude.
 
 
 
• **Ionosphere**
 
 
• The ionosphere is located between 80 and 400 km above the mesopause.
 
• It contains electrically charged particles known as ions, and hence, it is known as the ionosphere.
